_note: Subjects in this course pack. 'years' is the year of a UK optometry degree the subject is usually taught in (from 17 universities' published syllabi, see universities.json). Outline subjects list their topics before the full content is written. Students can rename a subject; the rename is saved per user.

themes.Foundations: The science underneath: optics, anatomy, how vision works
themes.Management: Clinical management: dispensing, refraction, contact lenses, binocular vision, paediatrics
themes.Patient: Examining the patient: anterior eye, posterior eye, diagnosis

modules.name: Optics & Ophthalmic Lenses
outline: Light, refraction and Snell's law; prisms and deviation
Vergence and the thin lens equation; lens power in dioptres
Thick lenses, cardinal points and back vertex power
Mirrors and reflection
Visual optics: the schematic eye, ametropia, far and near points
Astigmatism, cylindrical lenses, spherocylinder notation and transposition
Accommodation, presbyopia and reading additions
Aberrations, and physical optics: interference, diffraction and polarisation

modules.name: Ocular Anatomy & Physiology
outline: Orbit, eyelids and the lacrimal system
Cornea, conjunctiva and the tear film
Uvea, and aqueous production and drainage
Crystalline lens and accommodation
Retina: layers, photoreceptors and phototransduction
Visual pathway: optic nerve, chiasm, LGN and visual cortex
Extraocular muscles and cranial nerves
Blood supply of the eye and orbit

modules.name: Visual Perception & Vision Science
outline: Visual acuity and contrast sensitivity
Colour vision and colour vision deficiency
Light and dark adaptation
Visual fields
Depth perception and stereopsis
Motion, form and visual illusions
Psychophysics: thresholds and how they are measured

modules.name: Refraction & Management of Refractive Error
outline: Retinoscopy refinement and working-distance lens
Subjective refraction: best vision sphere, fogging, duochrome
Jackson cross-cylinder: axis then power
Binocular balancing (Humphriss immediate contrast, prism dissociation)
Accommodation: amplitude (push-up), lag, near point
Presbyopia and near add determination (age guide, plus-build-up, range of clear vision)
Prescribing decisions: when to change, partial prescribing, anisometropia
Presbyope clinic: running a full refraction on a real presbyopic patient

modules.name: Contact Lenses
outline: Keratometry and corneal topography for lens selection
Soft lens materials: hydrogel vs silicone hydrogel, water content, Dk and Dk/t
Soft lens fitting assessment: centration, movement, push-up test, coverage
RGP fitting and fluorescein patterns (alignment, steep, flat)
Choosing lens power: vertex distance correction above ±4.00 D
Care regimes, hygiene and patient instruction (insertion, removal)
Aftercare and complications: CLPU, CLARE, microbial keratitis, neovascularisation, GPC
Grading scales (Efron / CCLRU) and recording findings

modules.name: Anterior Eye Examination
outline: Slit lamp illumination techniques: diffuse, direct focal, parallelepiped, optic section, specular, retro-illumination, sclerotic scatter
Systematic anterior segment examination: lids, lashes, conjunctiva, cornea, AC, iris, lens
Van Herick anterior chamber angle grading
Fluorescein and lissamine green staining; grading corneal staining
Tear film assessment: TBUT, NIBUT, tear meniscus, Schirmer
Lid eversion technique
Common conditions: blepharitis, MGD, dry eye, conjunctivitis types

modules.name: Posterior Eye (and Glaucoma)
outline: Direct ophthalmoscopy technique
Indirect fundus examination with slit lamp and Volk lens
Optic disc assessment: size, cup-to-disc ratio, neuroretinal rim, ISNT rule
Macula and retinal vessels: what normal looks like
Tonometry: Goldmann applanation and non-contact
Glaucoma risk factors and referral criteria (check NICE / College guidance)
Fundus photography and OCT basics

modules.name: Diagnosis & Systemic Disease
outline: Case history and diagnostic reasoning
Building a differential diagnosis
Diabetes and the eye
Hypertension and the eye
Interpreting clinical data in PC-lab cases
Referral urgency and writing referrals

modules.name: Binocular Vision
outline: Heterophoria and heterotropia
Cover test
Fixation disparity and Mallett unit
Convergence insufficiency
Prism prescribing basics

modules.name: Paediatrics
outline: Visual development
Assessing vision in children (preferential looking, Kay pictures, Cardiff cards)
Cycloplegic refraction
Amblyopia
Myopia onset and myopia management

modules.name: Vision Science & Evidence
outline: Research design
Descriptive and inferential statistics
Reading and critiquing a paper
Evidence-based practice
Using the library and literature search

modules.name: Professional & Personal Development
outline: GOC Standards for Optical Students
Communication and consent
Interprofessional learning (IPL)
Reflective practice

modules.name: Duty of Candour
outline: What the professional duty of candour requires
Apologising and explaining when things go wrong
Raising concerns

modules.name: Public Health & Eye Health
outline: Causes of sight loss in the UK
Health inequalities and access to eye care
Health promotion in practice
Task A (see drop-in, week 11)

modules.name: Ocular Pharmacology & Therapeutics
outline: How topical eye drops reach their target (pharmacokinetics)
Diagnostic drugs: mydriatics, cycloplegics, anaesthetics and stains
Adverse reactions and contraindications, including angle-closure risk
Exemptions and the legal framework for optometrists using medicines
Anti-infectives and anti-inflammatories
Glaucoma medicines
Systemic medicines with eye side effects

modules.name: Low Vision
outline: Causes and impact of visual impairment in the UK
Low vision assessment: history, acuity, contrast and fields
Magnification: types and working out how much is needed
Magnifiers, telescopes and electronic aids
Lighting, contrast and non-optical aids
Certification (CVI), registration and referral to support services

modules.name: Clinical Learning in Practice (Placement Year)
outline: How the final placement year is structured
Building your log of patient episodes
Running a full routine eye examination on your own
Referral letters and communicating with GPs and hospital eye services
Record keeping, consent and safeguarding in practice
Preparing for final assessments and GOC registration

modules.name: Glaucoma, Medical Retina & Prescribing
outline: College of Optometrists higher certificates in glaucoma and medical retina
Glaucoma: risk factors, assessment and monitoring
Medical retina: AMD, diabetic retinopathy and vein occlusions
Acute and emergency eye care services
Additional supply and supplementary prescribing
Independent prescribing: the law, management plans and responsibility
